title: Theo and the Postcard
premise: Tamsin Zhou has built a careful, invisible life ghostwriting other people's triumphs, including the memoirs of her former best friend and rival, Celeste, who stole the credit for the novel that nearly destroyed Tamsin. When a family reunion threatens to expose how far she's fallen, Tamsin hires Theo Marsh, a warm, guarded ex-investigative journalist turned bartender, to pose as her boyfriend — but the fake date curdles into something real by dessert. Theo, it turns out, has his own unfinished business: a decade-old wrongful conviction his family suffered, tied to evidence that implicates Celeste's late publisher. As Tamsin ghostwrites Celeste's memoir, she uncovers the buried proof that could clear Theo's brother's name, forcing her to choose between the justice she can deliver anonymously and the revenge she's craved for years. In the end, Tamsin publishes the truth under her own name — sacrificing her ghostwriting career and her claim on her stolen novel — forgives the person in the mirror, and chooses Theo, whose brother walks free as the book closes on a postcard Theo finally sends to the address he'd been too afraid to write.
about_author: Hazel Sterling is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years listening to other people's confessions before writing her own. She lives in a coastal town in Oregon, where she collects postcards from strangers and answers every one.

chapters.title: The Address Nobody Writes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ghostwriting Celeste's glittering memoir by day and eating instant noodles by night, Tamsin receives a postcard with no return address — only a sentence from her own abandoned novel. The beat: quiet dread that her past has found her.

chapters.title: Invitation, Regrets Only
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her mother calls: the Zhou family reunion, all aunts and cousins and pointed questions about her 'successful writing career.' Tamsin invents a boyfriend on the spot. The beat: panic disguised as confidence.

chapters.title: The Man Who Pours Slow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She recruits Theo, the observant bartender at her usual dive, who agrees for reasons he won't explain. Their interview over closing-time drinks crackles with mutual suspicion and unexpected ease. The beat: reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Rehearsing a Lie
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. They rehearse their backstory in his empty bar — how they met, why he loves her — and Theo finds the lies too easy to say. He withholds his real motive: a name he recognizes from her ghostwriting client list. The beat: guilty attraction.

chapters.title: Arrivals
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The reunion begins; Theo charms her mother, disarms her sharp-tongued grandmother, and plays the boyfriend so well it stings. Celeste texts, demanding the memoir draft by month's end. The beat: the fake feels dangerously real.

chapters.title: Too Real by Dessert
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Over her aunt's almond cake, Tamsin's cover story about her 'novel' unravels — and Theo improvises a defense of her unfinished book that sounds like belief. She flees to the porch; he follows. The beat: the mask slips, on both sides.

chapters.title: What Theo Buried
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Alone, Theo studies an old clipping: his brother Daniel, convicted of arson in a fire that killed publisher Marcus Vane. The publisher's name also appears in Celeste's memoir materials. The beat: his fake date has become his investigation.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Transcribing Celeste's dictated chapters, Tamsin notices a gap — the summer of the Vane fire, glossed over in a single polished paragraph. Her journalist instincts, long dormant, wake up. The beat: suspicion sharpened by old betrayal.

chapters.title: Second Dates Are for Liars
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The reunion over, Theo keeps showing up — 'for credibility.' They fall into a rhythm of real conversations disguised as fake ones. Tamsin admits, obliquely, that someone stole her novel. The beat: intimacy arriving through confession.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo visits Daniel in prison and lies that he's 'close to something.' Flashback to the family's collapse after the conviction — their mother's death, the price of surviving an unjust verdict. The beat: grief hardened into obsession.

chapters.title: Celeste, Dictated
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A recording session with Celeste turns into a duel; Celeste needles Tamsin about her 'failed' novel while Tamsin probes the fire summer. Celeste deflects — but a name slips: Vane kept private files. The beat: cat and mouse in silk gloves.

chapters.title: Postcards, Plural
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. More unsigned postcards arrive, each quoting her stolen novel in order — someone out there remembers it better than she does. She realizes the sender is tied to Vane. The beat: the past is not past; it's corresponding.

chapters.title: The Fire File
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo traces Vane's estate and finds the files were boxed and stored — by Celeste's assistant. He tells Tamsin the truth about Daniel, braced for her to run. Instead she says: 'I can get us into that archive.' The beat: alliance, real at last.

chapters.title: Two Thieves, One Truth
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the estate archive, they find Vane's private correspondence — proof the fire was arson-for-insurance, and that Vane framed Daniel to silence him. Also: the manuscript Tamsin wrote, with Vane's note calling it 'the one Celeste will publish.' The beat: vindication and rage entwined.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo wants to take the file to a lawyer; Tamsin wants to detonate it publicly, destroying Celeste. Their first real fight: is justice outside the law still justice, or just revenge wearing its coat? The beat: love tested by old wounds.

chapters.title: The Memoir Deadline
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Celeste, suspicious, demands the final chapters in person and reveals she knows Tamsin has been 'asking about Marcus.' She offers Tamsin co-credit on the memoir — blood money. The beat: temptation with a familiar face.

chapters.title: The Mirror Chapter
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Writing Celeste's confession-by-proxy, Tamsin realizes she ghosted her own life the way she ghosts books — and that forgiving Celeste means first forgiving herself for surviving by disappearing. She writes the truest chapter she's ever written. The beat: the person in the mirror, faced at last.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The file leaks — not by them. Celeste's assistant, protecting herself, has sold it to a podcast. Daniel's case is suddenly news, but so are questions about who had access. Theo suspects Tamsin; she suspects him. The beat: trust cracking under pressure.

chapters.title: The Confrontation
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin confronts Celeste with everything — the stolen novel, the framed brother, the memoir built on Tamsin's invisible labor. Celeste offers a final deal: silence in exchange for restoring Tamsin's byline. The beat: the climax of the old wound.

chapters.title: Under Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin publishes an essay — her name on it — telling the whole story: the theft, the ghostwriting, the fire file. It costs her every client, including Celeste's memoir, and gains her something she'd forgotten she wanted: to be seen. The beat: the price of survival, finally paid.

chapters.title: The Verdict Outside the Courtroom
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Daniel's conviction is vacated; the state declines to retry. Theo waits at the prison gate with their father's coat and a postcard he never sent, addressed to the brother he refused to stop writing to. The beat: justice, imperfect and arriving anyway.

chapters.title: Return Address
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Months later, at the dive bar, Theo slides Tamsin a postcard — the first one he ever wrote her, unsent, confessing he'd known who she was from the start and stayed anyway. She writes her return address on it and hands it back. The beat: second chances, kept this time.
